_comment: C19 TRUST POLICY v3. v1 pinned GitHub's rotating OIDC JWKS leaves as an offline root, which was
wrong twice over. v2 fixed the anchor but left the IDENTITY POLICY able to FAIL OPEN: fields were
only checked when the caller happened to supply an expected value, so an identity carrying a wrong
source SHA, a wrong workflow digest and a wrong run URI verified with zero findings when those
expectations were absent - which is exactly how the real CLI called it.
v3 makes every delivery-standing field MANDATORY. A missing expectation is a refusal, never a skip.

tuf.provenance: https://tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev — root v15, snapshot v165, targets v14; the
tuf.provenanceNote: trusted root's digest equals the one the signed targets metadata declares.
tuf.freshnessNote: Sigstore's timestamp role expires within days by design. Historical bundle verification therefore checks signatures, thresholds and these minimum versions, NOT expiry: a package with a ten-year payload window must not stop verifying six days after it was built. Expiry IS enforced when this snapshot is refreshed from the Sigstore repository.

_comment: EXACT values only. A regex identity policy is how a verifier ends up accepting a signature
from a workflow it did not mean to trust — `.*` in the wrong place accepts any branch, any
workflow, or any fork. Every field below has one exact value, so there is nothing to widen.
identity._signerEventComment: the anchor workflow is workflow_run-triggered; the upstream ci run's own event is 'push' and is bound separately

sigstore-fulcio.description: Fulcio-issued short-lived certificate bound to a GitHub Actions OIDC identity, with the signature recorded in Rekor. The trust root is the TUF-authenticated Sigstore material, not any single rotating key.

local-dev.description: NON-DELIVERY test seam only. Controlled by the evidence process, therefore NOT independent. Hosted delivery standing refuses it by construction.

_requiredComment: Every field here MUST be present in the certificate AND matched against an expected value.
If the caller cannot supply an expectation, verification FAILS - it does not skip the check.
